targets.title: Using learner corpus methods in L2 acquisition research.
targets.evidence_quote: The aim of the current study is to replicate Lozano and Díaz-Negrillo’s reference study using a different dataset.
targets.outcome_quote: The reference study did not look into NTLU of 3rd person singular -s because of its low frequency, but the misuse errors for irregular past were reported to be similar to the current study (Lozano and Díaz-Negrillo 2019, 110). While the reference study discovered a partial U-shaped developmental pattern in the oversuppliance of regular past -ed (Lozano and Díaz-Negrillo 2019, 111), the current study 44 did not show such a pattern for this or any other morpheme.
targets.outcome_reasoning: No single overall replication verdict. The author explicitly reports both matching irregular-past error patterns and failure to recover the original U-shaped regular-past pattern. The central proficiency-order effect and article-error distribution also differ from the reference study. These are the two stated replication research questions, not incidental robustness analyses. Low frequencies limit some patterns but the author does not declare the entire attempt incapable of adjudication.

reasoning: Completed thesis tests one explicitly identified published reference study using a different learner sample from COREFL.
